claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: Lori's public statement, 'I have never seen Mason drink,' constitutes an out-of-court assertion by a declarant.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c)(1) - Hearsay requires a statement asserted by a declarant.
arguments.evidence_span: Lori's public statement, "I have never seen Mason drink."

arguments.text: The statement is offered 'on the issue of damage to Mason's reputation as a sober individual,' indicating it is proffered to prove the truth of the matter asserted (that Mason does not drink).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c)(2) - Hearsay requires the statement to be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of damage to Mason's reputation as a sober individual

arguments.text: There is no indication in the narrative that the statement is offered for a non-hearsay purpose (e.g., effect on listener, notice, or state of mind) or falls under a party-opponent exclusion, reinforcing its classification as hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) & 801(d)(2) - Absence of non-hearsay purpose or exclusion supports hearsay classification.
